amanda_cs: FYI customer (ACME) opened an escalation — their webhook consumer started failing JSON.parse() after our most recent model promotion. They only see this for json_mode/structured_output. Error: "Unexpected token '{' in JSON at position 0" on our webhook receiver side. Happened right after the v8.1 promotion.

maya_support: Can you paste a minimal request + the exact response body the customer receives? Also include x-request-id if available.

amanda_cs: Pasting example (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
 -d '{"model":"redwood/llm-v8.1","mode":"json_mode","input":"extract_orders"}'
```
Response body (what customer receives):
```json
{"orders":{"0":{"id":"ord_123","amount":99.5},"1":{"id":"ord_124","amount":49.0}}
```
Customer's strict JSON schema expects an array: "orders": [{...}] and their parser chokes because we returned an object with numeric keys.

jason_eng: :eyes: that's interesting — arrays turned into index-keyed objects. Do we have raw serving logs or the chunked stream? Any sign of streaming boundary markers being interpreted as JSON fragments? Please include request id.

amanda_cs: request id: req_8f3a2b. Raw stream (trimmed):
```
data: {"chunk": "["}
data: {"chunk":"{\"id\":\"ord_123\",\"amount\":99.5},"}
data: {"chunk":"{\"id\":\"ord_124\",\"amount\":49.0}]"}
```
Customer's receiver stitches those as one string then parses. But somehow the re-assembled value becomes object-shaped on their side.

li_dev: Quick hypothesis: during the v8.1 compilation we changed a chunk reassembly optimization for structured outputs that normalizes numeric-array-indices into maps when a chunk boundary lands inside an array element. In other words, we accidentally run a step that reconstructs arrays using map semantics when index tokens are observed. Not the same as truncation/trailing-comma — it's turning an array into {"0":...,"1":...}.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: promoted redwood/llm-v8.1 -> prod at 2026-02-15T03:12:04Z (canary promoted).

ryan_sre: If that's the case, we should reproduce locally against v8.0 and v8.1 and capture the full streaming frames. Also check our streaming-to-sse rewriter that previously coerced arrays to keyed objects in some edge-cases (we had a hotfix in 2025 for list-wrapping).

li_dev: I'll run a quick local against both variants — can someone add a minimal test harness? Here's a short curl-based repro using chunked streaming that should show the difference:
```bash
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-TEST' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood/llm-v8.1","mode":"json_mode","input":"emit_array_of_orders"}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream | sed -n '1,200p'
```
We should compare with v8.0. If v8.0 returns "orders": [ ... ] and v8.1 returns keyed-object, we have a regression.

maya_support: Customer is on a dedicated private stack (not hosted) and can't be instantly rolled back. They asked for a short-term mitigation on their consumer side. Any lightweight server-side patch we can push to dedicated instances?

amanda_cs: They tried a JSON normalization on their side that converts numeric-keyed objects to arrays, which fixes parsing but is brittle. They're asking us for a recommended fail-safe.

li_dev: Short-term mitigations: (1) recommend a tolerant parser on their webhook (convert numeric-keyed root objects to arrays), (2) enable our compatibility shim — we can flip a runtime flag on dedicated/private customers to disable the new chunk-normalizer. I'll prepare the flag and a safe rollout.

jason_eng: Long-term fix: update streaming reassembly to preserve original array tokens and ensure we never generate numeric-keyed objects from arrays. Add unit tests for chunk-split cases where array items span frames. Acceptance criteria: any json_mode output that semantically represents a JSON array must serialize as a JSON array in the final assembled stream for both chunked and non-chunked flows.

ryan_sre: Action items:
- li_dev: run A/B test across v8.0/v8.1 in staging with synthetic emit_array_of_orders payload and post logs to thread (due EOD).
- jason_eng: draft PR for streaming reassembly tests and the compatibility flag (WIP).
- maya_support/amanda_cs: provide customer-safe normalization snippet and confirm it's applied on their consumer webhook (I'll coordinate).

amanda_cs: I'll send the customer a snippet they can drop in while we investigate:
```js
// tolerant normalizer
function normalizeOrders(body) {
  if (body.orders && typeof body.orders === 'object' && !Array.isArray(body.orders)) {
    const keys = Object.keys(body.orders).sort((a,b)=>Number(a)-Number(b));
    if (keys.every(k => String(Number(k))===k)) {
      return {...body, orders: keys.map(k => body.orders[k])};
    }
  }
  return body;
}
```
They confirmed it unblocks them locally.

jason_eng: Good. Once li_dev posts logs, I'll cherry-pick the failing frame and add a reproduction test. If we confirm the chunk-normalizer is responsible, we'll patch and push a hotfix to dedicated/private customers and schedule a rollback for hosted canary if necessary.

li_dev: Posting initial staging comparison (summary): v8.0 -> orders array preserved; v8.1 -> array reconstructed as numeric-keyed object in 1/2000 requests where chunk boundary split an item early. Will upload detailed frames and request IDs shortly.

maya_support: Thanks — please tag me when the runtime flag is ready so I can coordinate with the customer. :thumbsup:

amanda_cs: I'll keep the customer updated and escalate to account team. Thanks team.
